## Why This Is Asked

Tests familiarity with basic bit manipulation and endianness handling in a realistic, atomic operation.

## Key Concepts

- 32-bit width handling
- Bit shifts and OR composition
- Endianness considerations

## Code Example

```c
uint32_t swapHalves32(uint32_t x) {
  return (x >> 16) | (x << 16);
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you generalize to 64-bit words?
- How would you implement with explicit masks for clarity and portability?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests mastery of bitwise rotations and edge-case handling without branches.

## Key Concepts
- Rotation vs shift
- Masking with 31 to limit r
- Avoid undefined behavior when r=0
- Portability of 32-bit unsigned types

## Code Example
```javascript
static inline uint32_t rotateRight32(uint32_t n, unsigned r) {
  r &= 31;
  return (n >> r) | (n << ((32 - r) & 31));
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you adapt for 64-bit rotation with zero-cost intrinsics?
- What compiler options ensure the operation is unsigned arithmetic?

Tests ability to apply simple bit-tricks succinctly and reason about edge cases without loops. It also shows understanding of bitwise adjacency relationships across 64 bits.

- Bitwise AND and right shift

## Why This Is Asked
Tests understanding of bitwise rotation, a common low-level primitive in systems and cryptography. 

## Key Concepts
- Bitwise rotation vs shift
- Normalizing k with k & 31
- Safe shifts using (32 - kk) & 31 to avoid 32-bit shifts

```c
uint32_t rotl32(uint32_t n, uint32_t k) {

}
```

- What are potential compiler/target differences in shifts?
